page0.text: When did I figure out the truth of that dream?

page1.text:
A desert as far as I can see.
The infinite swords stuck in the ground do not have a wielder.
The sky is stormy, and there is no forest or town or ocean in the far horizon.
The hill of swords that continues endlessly.
A graveyard of steel that has no user or owner.
I realized from the start...
That was the scenery inside that hero's mind.

page2.text: After a sequence of many events, one who becomes a Heroic Spirit ends up in that place.

page3.text:
There are those who left this world loved by many people, and those who left this world being praised as noble kings.
There are those who died in battle wishing to fight, and those who pass on after leading a long, fulfilling life.
...However, there seem to be many who were praised against their will.

page4.text:
If true heroes are those who legitimately earned their title, then these are different heroes.
They should be called Avenger, the anti-hero, that ended up in that place because of their reversed fate.
Those who are in the opposite position as heroes, yet worshipped as heroes as a result.
Even those who are treated as Heroic Spirits, who both hate and are hated by humans, are used as Guardians.

page5.text:
...But, he is in a gray area.
He's not a true hero nor a rare Avenger.
His efforts were unrewarded and his life ended in betrayal, but he never hated humans until the very end.
But, that too wore away.
Yes, he must have gotten worn out.

page6.text:
I was mistaken.
Heroic Spirits, familiars called Servants.
...Positioned as Guardians, the Counter Force of humanity.
They are summoned to various ages and prevent the destruction of the world.
But, the only condition they have is destruction caused by humans.
Destruction caused by nature and external factors are not solved by the Counter Force of humanity, but by that of the world.

page7.text:
...That is why the only thing that Heroic Spirits who become Guardians see is self-destruction.
An existence only to eliminate destruction created from human desires.
He made a contract with the world to save humans and became a hero.
In return, he became a Guardian after his death and was shown humanity's self-destruction over and over again.
He was summoned as a Heroic Spirit to save people, yet he has been forced to clean up after people's misconduct.

page8.text:
...It did not take long for him to start thinking that was in vain and he couldn't help despising the human world.
And in the end...
Even after he died, he kept on getting betrayed by the ideal that he protected.

page9.text:
"Rin. What happened? Do you feel dizzy?"
"Huh...?"
Rin Tohsaka wakes up, being called upon suddenly.
...She slowly looks around.
This is the foreigners' cemetery.
It's only past 7 PM, but it is deserted.
Well, the hill where the church stands is always deserted.

page10.text:
"...Sorry, I was sleeping. I seem to be a bit tired."
"That is understandable, you have not slept since last night. If you are not feeling well, shall we postpone this? There is no need to attack right now."
"...No, we can't take our time. We found out where Caster is, so we should settle this now."
Rin declares and notices that her body is warm.
It must be because her familiar, Archer, had protected her from the cold with his cloak.

page11.text:
"...Heh. You realized I was asleep. It's rude of you to not wake me up."
"Well, I do not see many people sleeping while standing. I had to observe since it was so rare."
"...That's even worse. Who are you to be staring at a girl's sleeping face?"

page12.text:
"Do not worry, I swear that I have not done such a rude thing.
But, I did hear something. I can close my eyes if I try, but that does not work for my ears."
"...I see. Did I say something, Archer?"
"Yeah. You muttered several unsettling things, like how you were displeased and pissed off."

page13.text:
"...Oh, okay."
Rin sighs with relief.
The dream that she just saw cannot be discussed.
She can't have Archer know about it.
She likes their relationship.
...In order to maintain that, she must hide the fact that she knows Archer's past.

page14.text:
"Let's go, Archer. I know a bit about the church. I have an idea of where she may be hiding."
She brushes away Archer's cloak and stands up.
Archer protects her back silently.
Then...
"Hey, Archer. Have you ever regretted what you have done?"
She asks without turning around.

page15.text:
...
"If possible, I don't want to until the end. Even when I've really been beaten, I want to grit my teeth and be stubborn.
But, I bet that's hard. Harder than I can imagine, I suppose."

page16.text:
"That kind of idealism depends on the person.
There are some who can and some who can't. You are the former. Those kinds of people do not make any mistakes and do not think about their own mistakes."

page17.text:
"...Hey, you make it sound like I'm some kind of brazen tyrant."
"That is good self-awareness, Rin.
A vibrant person shines brighter than others.
Those kinds of people never grit their teeth.
...So. This is my personal opinion, but you are definitely one of those people. Rin Tohsaka believes in her own path until the end."

page18.text:
The knight in the red cloak says, as if singing.
Rin blushes at his answer, and asks her main question to him without looking back.

page19.text:
"...Then what about you? Do you believe that you're correct until the very end?"
"Hm? I'm sorry, but that question is meaningless."
"...Why? That's not something you can't answer, right?"
Her voice is slightly nervous.

page20.text:
To that...
"The 'until the very end' part is meaningless.
Did you forget, Master?
My final moment ended long ago."
The red knight answers in a dry voice.
